summary: The candidate implements the opt-in OpenAI request-metrics feature and fixes the reported prompt=["first","second"], n=1 loss when every emitted choice has measured timing data. Its focused completion, chat, and timing tests pass. It does not fully preserve per-choice association: both completion serializers filter choices whose metrics object is empty, so a two-choice response can carry a one-element request_metrics list with no way to identify which choice it belongs to. This is a partial fix rather than a full resolution of the reviewed contract.
remaining_counterexamples: For a two-choice completion where choice 0 has no positive timing values and choice 1 has e2e_latency=2.5, the normal response contains two choices but sglext.request_metrics=[{"e2e_latency":2.5}]. Positional per-choice association is lost. The same filtering pattern is present in the streaming completion and chat serializers.

tests.command: On prepared base 358c163, temporarily use the candidate completion regression tests and run: PYTHONPATH=/job/repo/python /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-a075ff9bc8b2/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_completions.py -k 'batched_prompt_metrics_preserve_all_choices or batched_prompt_metrics_cardinality_multiplies_by_n'
tests.what_was_measured: Prepared-base failure in actual non-streaming handler/JSON serialization, streaming generator/SSE serialization, and 2 prompts x n=2 response construction: choices were emitted but sglext metrics were absent.

170 tests and 70 subtests passed, including candidate regressions for normal and streaming completions, prompt cardinality multiplied by n, chat metrics, opt-in propagation, opt-out omission, scalar single-choice shape, and timing conversion.

tests.command: At exact candidate 0e629c84, invoke OpenAIServingCompletion._build_completion_response with two choices, the first without positive timing fields and the second with e2e_latency=2.5, then assert metrics cardinality equals choice cardinality.
tests.what_was_measured: Independent adversarial serialization case produced choices=2 and metrics=1, proving positional per-choice association is not preserved when a choice has an empty metrics object.
Candidate source and tests have no whitespace errors; candidate-retained historical evidence files were intentionally excluded.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X (ROCm 7.2, Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2) was visible, but this review exercised Python serving/serialization with deterministic generated outputs and did not claim an unrelated GPU numerical smoke as HTTP evidence. No model weights path was provided for a live model-backed server.

remaining_limitations: No model weights path was supplied, so a live model-backed HTTP server was not launched. Actual Python OpenAI handler and serialization methods were exercised with deterministic tokenizer-manager outputs.
The candidate changes no C, C++, HIP, CUDA, FlyDSL, or header files; repository-environment.json declares native=null, so no native rebuild was applicable.
The prepared architecture is x86_64 with one AMD Instinct MI350X under ROCm 7.2. The embedded Rust server remains outside the original issue's stated initial scope.
Only the demonstrated partial-metrics association counterexample blocks full acceptance; the originally reviewed all-measured multi-prompt n=1 and prompt_count x n cases pass.
